li.span: Four DAX-based OLE DB queries expose controlled semantic-model outputs to the Excel scenario modeller. The resulting Excel tables form a stable interface between the semantic model, user-facing configuration sheets, and Python modules.

span.span: Case listing, profiles and tax datasets are loaded into Python for validation and scenario processing, while the summarised Totals & Avgs dataset remains an Excel-only decision-support layer.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 392px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1099px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

li.span: Governed access: Excel consumes controlled semantic-model outputs rather than accessing source data directly
Purpose-specific extraction: queries return only the data required by each modelling function
Single source of truth: common semantic-model logic supports consistent downstream analysis
Separation of concerns: data retrieval remains distinct from scenario configuration and calculation

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 392px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1099px; margin-left: 438px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

li.span: Transparent interfaces: defined queries make data movement and transformation inspectable
Consistent structures: standardised outputs provide predictable inputs to Excel and Python
Data minimisation: only required attributes, metrics and periods are transferred
Reusable integration: common interface patterns support maintainable downstream datasets
